patients.label: 49-year-old woman with recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa and IgA nephropathy undergoing peritoneal dialysis catheter replacement under subcostal TAPB
attribution_limitations: The Case presentation calls airway blistering following critical airway obstruction and difficult airway "potential", while the Discussion states general anesthesia was avoided because of the "presence" of difficult airway and critical airway obstruction.

Case text mentions incision points A, B and D; the figure caption lists incisions A to E, and the text does not describe points C and E or which incision belongs to which catheter beyond A to B (original catheter) and D (left side).
The case gives blood albumin 1.9 g/dL without a flag; the Discussion says this patient developed hypoalbuminemia (1.9 g/dL) without identifying the measurement or its time.

Postoperative image of the surgery site. The incision points and course of removed (light blue arrow) and newly inserted (blue arrow) peritoneal dialysis catheters are shown. The red dot and arrow along the subcostal oblique line indicate the injection point and course of local anesthesia via subcostal transversus abdominis plane block. The light-red coloration indicates the expected analgesic area

She needed peritoneal dialysis catheter replacement.

claims.text: The original catheter was removed and a new catheter placed in the left abdominal wall. Moderate pain at incision point A on the non-blocked side and mild pain at point D on the blocked side were managed with additional lidocaine, intravenous fentanyl and ketamine; repeated low-dose fentanyl was given for peritoneal manipulation without visceral pain.
